title: Saving the level
description:
Save and load the state of a level: the map, the player and the monsters.

```
save -> level.sav (map 5x7, player (3, 1), 2 monsters)
load -> identical state (checked field by field)
version 1 file loaded by version 2 -> monsters get default hp
```
hints: `<sstream>` gives streams over strings. `std::istringstream in{ text };` reads from a string exactly like `std::cin` (`in >> word >> number`, or `std::getline(in, line)` for one line at a time), and its condition is false once a read fails. `std::ostringstream out; out << "x " << 5; out.str()` builds a string the way `std::cout` prints.
Write counts before lists (`rows 3`, `monsters 1`) so the reader knows how many lines follow (lesson 11.06).
Check the version first and refuse files newer than the program understands.
requirements: A text format with a version line first.
Write and read the map rows, the player and each monster with its hp.
A loaded state compares equal to the saved one (`operator==` defaulted).
stretch: Save in binary and compare the file sizes.
